To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and validated a simple, fast, sensitive and selective analytical method by GC-MS to quantify methyl dihydorjasmonate in microemulsions, and we demonstrated that microemulsions can be a promising delivery system for methyl dihydrojasmonic acid to tumor cells.
we have developed and characterized a new formulation of methyl dihydrojasmonic acid, which is a promising nanocarrying system for drug delivery.
a simple, sensitive and reproducible analytical method was developed to quantify MJ from MEs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical method by GC-MS to quantify the drug compound, the physicochemical characterization of MEs loaded with MJ and its in vitro release.
the development of a new analytical method to quantify MJ in ME formulations and to study the release of the drug from the systems.
the development of an analytical method to detect and quantify MJ in MEs, and the physicochemical characterization of these systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MEs loaded with MJ are promising drug delivery systems for the controlled release of MJ.
the developed method is effective to quantify low and higher concentrations of MJ in different formulations and can be applied in different studies involving the drug compound.
the ME formulation is an excellent nanocarrier to improve the aqueal solubility, and to increase the release rate of the MJ, which can be a promising drug for cancer chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analytical method developed for quantitative determination of methyl dihydrojasmonic acid (MDHA) was suitable for detection and quantification of the drug compound from the ME formulations.
the analytical method developed for quantification of the drug compound from MEs in the release test is suitable for detection and quantification of low and high concentrations.

the developed analytical method can be applied for the quantitative determination and characterization of MJ from different compositions of microemulsions, as well as for the in vitro release studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analytical method developed for quantification of MJ in MEs is suitable for detecting and quantifying the drug compound from the different formulations of MEs used in in vitro studies.
we developed an analytical method to quantify methyl jasmonate in oil-in-water micro-emulsions.
the developed ME formulation can be a promising drug delivery system for MJ, and it can be applied in the treatment of cancer.
